title: Staged Rollout: Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private Pathway
content:
Purpose:
This working proposal describes a pragmatic, instrumented pathway for customers to start on Redwood Hosted, transition to Dedicated capacity, and — if required by compliance or latency geography — move to Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. The goal is to make the migration low-risk for the customer and low-effort for Redwood ops/SE, with measurable gates and rollback plans.

Context / Why this variant: quick wins + safe migration
- Many customers want to validate application-level correctness and UX quickly (hosted) but later require predictable throughput (dedicated) or data isolation (private).
- A staged pathway reduces upfront engineering commitment for customers while enabling Redwood to capture usage and then propose capacity/contract conversions.
- This doc is intentionally concrete: includes routing patterns, SLO gates, security checklist, and an ops-runbook for each phase.

High-level design summary (textual diagram):
PHASE A: Hosted (dev -> prod trial)
  - Customer connects to Redwood API (api.redwood.ai) using org key
  - Use hosted model variant with standard KV cache and auto-batching
  - Collect metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens per request, cache hit-rate, error rate, cost per 1M tokens

PHASE B: Dedicated (reserved pool)
  - Create tenant-specific Dedicated pool behind same API surface (routing tag: dedicated:tenant-XX)
  - Route production traffic gradually (canary 5/20/100) using rollout policy in Console
  - Enable capacity-based autoscale and pre-warming windows for daily peak

PHASE C: Private (VPC or on-prem)
  - Customer obtains a Private deployment package or Redwood provisions VPC peered endpoint
  - Control plane remains in Redwood (optionally private control plane for high-compliance customers)
  - Data path either stays within customer VPC or via on-prem appliance

Transition mechanics (how traffic moves):
- Canary policy: start 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%; each step requires passing gate checks (see Gate criteria).
- Fallback rules: immediate fallback to hosted variant on 5xx spike >0.5% for >10m or p99 latency breach >2x baseline for >10m.
- Session affinity: for chat workloads with long context, route the same user/session to the same backend to preserve KV cache locality during migration window.

Gate criteria between phases (must be met before increasing traffic):
1) Reliability: error rate <= 0.2% (5xx + transport errors) over 30m.
2) Latency: p99 dedicated/private <= hosted_p99 * 1.25 OR absolute p99 <= 1200ms (whichever stricter).
3) Cost delta: expected cost per token not > +30% unless SLA demands justify it.
4) Functional conformity: prompt/response diffs: sample 1k requests, regressions <= 1% (manual review of top-10 failure modes).
5) Observability: traces, token-level cost breakdown, and structured logs active for the tenant.

Operational checklist by phase:
PHASE A (Hosted):
- Confirm org API key and usage limits
- Enable enterprise logging export (s3/kinesis) if requested
- Seed canonical prompt set for quality evals
- Baseline metrics capture for 48–72 hours

PHASE B (Dedicated):
- Provision pool: GPU type, instance count, reserved throughput
- Configure routing tag and canary policy in Console
- Set up per-pool autoscaler and warmup policy (cron for scheduled spikes)
- IAM keys: rotate from test keys to production keys; store service account in customer's secret manager if required
- Security: ensure private subnet egress rules for model pulls (if required) and KMS integration for model artifacts

PHASE C (Private):
- Network: validate VPC peering or VPN, MTU, egress restrictions, and NAT/firewall rules
- Key management: integrate customer KMS/HSM where required; rotate keys during handoff
- Audit: enable audit log ingestion to customer SIEM; confirm retention SLAs
- Local infra: verify GPU drivers, OS patch baseline, and local monitoring agents are installed

Rollback and incident playbook (short):
- Canary fails during step -> immediate rollback to previous traffic step; if persistent -> abort migration and revert all new routing rules
- Major outage on Dedicated/Private: fail traffic to Hosted with a tombstone policy that labels requests during incident for postmortem sampling
- Postmortem: capture sample transcripts (redact PII), topology at failure, and model variant identifiers

Security & compliance notes:
- Data residency: Hosted satisfies many customers but not those requiring all inference data to remain in customer VPC/on-prem. Private is the only path for full isolation.
- Encryption: require TLS+mutual-TLS for private connections. KMS integration required for private model artifacts.
- Auditability: expose request/response hashes (not raw content) to customer audit store; raw transcripts only on explicit opt-in and with access controls.

Cost model (back-of-envelope)
- Hosted: unit cost X (baseline) -> includes multi-tenant pooling and cross-customer efficiency.
- Dedicated: base contract monthly + usage; expect +20-40% unit cost vs hosted due to reserved capacity and lower bin-packing.
- Private: CAPEX/OPEX for on-prem; VPC-hosted private likely +50–120% unit cost depending on utilization and region.
(Engineering note: we will fill numeric estimates per GPU type using infra estimator template during handoff.)

Quality gating and evaluation plan:
- Define 500–1,000 representative prompt pairs (training set vs production corpus) as canary tests.
- Run A/B comparison: Hosted (control) vs Dedicated/Private (candidate) with automatic diffing and sampling of mismatches for manual review.
- Track semantic similarity score and failure class taxonomy (hallucination, truncation, missing-tool-calls).

POC success criteria (customer-facing):
- Functional parity: 95% of sampled requests within acceptable similarity threshold
- Latency: 90th/95th percentile latency within agreed SLO
- Cost: predicted monthly bill within +/-20% of estimate or having committed discount
- Ops readiness: automated alerting and paging configured; runbook validated with 1 simulated failover

Workshop notes (what to cover with customer during kickoff):
- Business drivers: why migrate? (latency, cost predictability, data isolation)
- Peak patterns: hourly/daily/weekly concurrency and tail latency expectations
- Compliance: any data residency or cert requirements (SOC2, HIPAA, etc.)
- Integration points: destination for logs/metrics, SIEM, secret stores, and networking contacts
- Timeline: 2–6 week POC typical but depends on network and security review

Open questions / risks (needs follow-up):
- Does the customer require a private control plane or is private data path sufficient?
- How tolerant is the app to transient model-version drift during migration? (need explicit acceptance)
- If customer traffic is dominated by long-chat sessions, we need a strategy for KV-cache migration or sticky-routing beyond simple canary percentages.

Action items (owners):
- Priya: prepare infra cost estimate and dedicated pool sizing template (due +3 business days)
- Liam: draft network checklist and VPC peering runbook (due +5 days)
- Mei: assemble representative prompt set with customer and run initial baseline tests (due +7 days)
- Diego: create canary rollout policy in Console and test rollback logic in staging (due +4 days)

Notes to self / internal shorthand:
- Keep migration button available in Console; add explicit ‘force-fallback-to-hosted’ toggle
- Consider adding telemetry tag that records which pool served each response for easy billing reconciliation
- Keep private control-plane ask on sale radar — often negotiation point for enterprise legal

Appendix: quick runbook snippet (for on-call)
- Symptom: p99 spike on Dedicated after 20% traffic shift
  1) Validate: check pool health + GPU utilization + OOM errors
  2) If utilization < 90% and no errors, rollback to 5% and notify infra team
  3) If OOM or infra fault -> failover to Hosted and open SE incident

- Symptom: auth failures when switching to Private endpoint
  1) Confirm mTLS certs and KMS keys present and valid
  2) Validate VPC routing + firewall logs
  3) Fallback: switch traffic to Hosted until fix complete
